confusions: The debt bar chart says it uses IMF figures while the text quotes 101.3% and the OECD's 92.5%, so I could not tell which UK debt number to trust.
The 'Work' section only gave one figure for everyone aged 16 to 64, and I could not find the 25 to 34 or 18 to 24 numbers from 1992.
The richest fifth had a 46.0% figure for share of all taxes and a 36.2% figure for share of income, and I got muddled about which one was which.
The Who pays page says HMRC and the ONS count different people and taxes and to keep them apart, which made the numbers hard to compare.
The top 1% section mixes share of Income Tax with share of income in rows that look alike, and I was not sure which row answered my question.
Japan's net interest figure was -0.1% and the page said a figure below zero meant the government got more than it paid, which I did not follow.
The pages are very long and I was scrolling in big jumps, so I probably skipped bits of text such as the rest of the borrowing-cost explanation.
I ran out of actions before reaching the immigration, defence, welfare, housing and high-earner pages, so I could not answer those questions.
